newsitem.title: EGYPT: Spanish king bringing business people to Egypt. [CORRECTED 16:45 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Spanish king bringing business people to Egypt. [CORRECTED 16:45 GMT]

text.p: King Juan Carlos will bring 50 Spanish business people to Cairo next week for what the Spanish government hopes will be an opportunity to drum up business.

"The visit is going to be a turning-point in economic relations...Egypt is taking off but many Spanish business people have not yet realised what is happening," embassy economic counsellor Miguel Iriso told a briefing on Thursday.
The economic highlight of the king's three-day visit will be a "business encounter" on February 19 when Spanish business people will meet 60 to 70 Egyptian businessmen.
"It will be a chance for the Spanish to find out about Egypt. Standard and Poor's has just given Egypt an investment-grade rating, a very good sign," Iriso added.
Speakers will include King Juan Carlos, Egyptian Public Enterprise Minister Atef Obeid, Economy Minister Nawal el-Tatawi and possibly Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri.
Iriso said Spain had fallen behind other countries in exporting to Egypt but had done better in investment.
The biggest Spanish investor is oil company Repsol, which has invested $500 million in Egypt and plans to invest another $500 million in gas, he said.
Spain, which has the ninth largest national economy in the world, is only the 13th largest source of Egyptian imports, holding two percent of the market.

"We think we should do better...So the foreign ministry is considering financial help in the form of soft loans so that our companies can compete with those of other countries that do offer soft loans," Iriso added.

King Juan Carlos, on his first state visit to Egypt since 1977, is bringing Foreign Minister Abel Matutes, Secretary of State for Cooperation Fernando Villalonga (corrects title) and Secretary of State for Trade and Tourism Jose Manuel Fernandez Norniella.
The king and queen will arrive on Monday and leave for a private visit to the southern resort of Luxor on Thursday. The king will have talks with President Hosni Mubarak on Tuesday.
